sentences.text: It is no longer res integra that succession petitions are to be decided summarily.

Sec. 373 of the Indian Succession Act provides that a succession petition is to be decided in a summary manner and even if court cannot decide the right to the certificate without determining questions of law or fact which may seem to be too complicated and difficult for determination in a summary proceedings,
T.K. Bose vs State (Nct Of Delhi) on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82890038/
3

entities.text: T.K. Bose vs State (Nct Of Delhi)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the Court may nevertheless grant a certificate to a person if he appears to be the person having prima facie the best title thereto.
Thus U/s. 373 of Indian Succession Act, only prima facie case is to be seen and other questions of law and fact which may be complicated are to be decided by a regular civil court.
14. In the case of Madhvi Amma Bhawani Amma and others Vs. Kunjikutty Pillai Meenakshi Pillai and others, Respondents.

entities.text: Madhvi Amma Bhawani Amma and others Vs. Kunjikutty Pillai Meenakshi Pillai and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
AIR 2000 Supreme Court 2301=2000 AIR SCW 2432 it was held that sub-sec. (3) of S. 373 of Succession Act which deals with procedure for grant of certificate reveals two things;
"...first adjudication is in a summarily proceedings and secondly if the question of law and fact are intricate or difficult, it could still grant the said certificate based on applicants prima facie title.
In other words the grant of certificate under it is only a determination of prima facie title.
This as a necessary corollary confirms that it is not a final decision between the parties.
So, it cannot be construed that mere grant of such certificate or a decision in such proceeding would constitute to be decision on an issue finally decided between the parties.

If that be so how could principle of res judicata be made applicable to a case in a subsequent suit?".
15.
Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 provides that when a Hindu male dies intestate, his property shall first devolve upon the Class-I legal heirs specified in The Schedule of the Act.

Mother,
widow, son and daughter are class-I legal heirs as per the Schedule.
It is categorically stated by PW-5 that the Petition no. SC/44/2020 T.K. Bose Vs. State & Anr. 6/8 deceased was married and died issueless.

entities.text: Petition no. SC/44/2020 T.K. Bose Vs. State & Anr. 6/8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is categorically stated by PW-5 that the wife of the deceased predeceased the deceased.
It is also categorically stated that mother of the deceased predeceased the deceased.
As such, there is no class-I legal heirs of the deceased.

As per the section, if there is no class-I legal heir,
than the property devolves upon the class-II legal heirs of the deceased.
As per the section, father falls in the category of Class- II, sub class-(I).
However, it is categorically stated by PW-5 that father of the deceased had also expired.
It is stated by PW-5 that the petitioners No. 1 & 3 and respondent no. 2 Sh. B.C. Bose are the brothers and sister of the deceased.

Furthermore, the sister, namely,
Meena Ray of the deceased had expired on 18.08.2020 i.e. after the death of the deceased, leaving behind her LR, namely, Moinik Ray and Samrat Ray.
However, Samrat Ray had also expired on 15.05.2014 unmarried and also had not adopted any child and Moinik Ray is petitioner No. 2 in the present petition.

As per the schedule to the Hindu Succession Act read with Section 8 of the Act, the petitioners No. 1 and 3, namely, T.K. Bose and Hena Dutta and respondent no. 2, namely, B.C. Bose being brothers and sister of the deceased fall in Class II, Entry II (3) and (4).
Whereas, the petitioner no. 2, namely, Moinik Ray falls in Class II, Entry IV (2), being the sister's son.
Furthermore, it is admitted fact that sister, namely. Meena Ray had also expired after the death of the deceased leaving behind one son, namely. Moinik Ray.
As such, petitioner no. 2 is also entitled to get succession certificate as the succession was opened at the time of death of sister of the deceased.

Hence,
petitioners No. 1 to 3 and respondent no. 2 are entitled to grant of Succession Certificate.
